subject: Response bands and measurement proposal for hosted API commitments

Cc: procurement@finline.com
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify p50/p95 commitments + measurement window for Hosted API

Hi Hannah,

We're finalizing procurement for our new patient-data enrichment pipeline and need to lock down latency commitments for Redwood's hosted API before legal signs off. Two quick asks:

1) Can you confirm the proposed p50 and p95 numeric targets you can commit to for the hosted tier (single-region US)?
2) How are those quantiles measured? Specifics we need: measurement window (sliding vs fixed), sampling cadence, regional aggregation, and whether transient carveouts (maintenance/burst) are excluded.

We're HIPAA-adjacent and need clarity on measurement so we can map to our operational alerts. If you have a short draft we can attach to the contract, please send.

Thanks,
Carlos Vega
Head of Procurement
Finline Health

(Attachment: Finline-SLA-questions.docx)

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 commitments + measurement window for Hosted API

Carlos — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a short draft (RDW-SLA-draft-v1.pdf) with two commitment tiers and measurement rules. High level here so you have immediate answers while we iterate:

- Standard (hosted): p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 320ms (US region)
- Premium (hosted + reserved patching): p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 220ms

Measurement model proposed in the draft (summary):
- Rolling sliding-window measurement: p50/p95 computed over a 1-hour sliding window sampled every 5 minutes (so windows overlap).
- Per-region aggregation: quantiles computed per region (US-East, US-West) and reported at the regional level.
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance and proven downstream provider outages are excluded. Short transient spikes from large burst loads are handled by a documented transient carveout policy (limited hours per quarter).

Engineering (Karthik) will share more on sampling and how batching/KV cache affects observed latency. Ben will follow up with commercial credit proposals. Happy to hop on a 30m call to walk the team through the draft.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: RDW-SLA-draft-v1.pdf)

Quick tech note for the record and for Finline:

Proposed measurement mechanics (rationale + details):
- Sliding 1-hour window sampled every 5 minutes (we evaluate the p50/p95 of requests within each 1h window). Sampling cadence gives us noise reduction while preserving responsiveness to degradations.
- We report the worst regional value for commitment checks (i.e., customer gets the region-level view relevant to their traffic footprint).
- Batching and KV-cache influence: as request mix changes, measured tail moves. To avoid penalizing a customer for cold-start cache misses and realistic load shape changes, we:
  * Exclude the first N minutes after a canary/rollout or model variant swap (warmup carveout).
  * Allow temporary burst carveouts: maximum of 8 hours per region per calendar quarter, gated by incident review.
- Synthetic probes vs production sampling: commitments are based on production traffic. Synthetic probes are used for alerting but not for SLA calculation.

Exception policy (short):
- For one-off infra incidents > threshold, automatic credit applied if we cannot meet p95 for > 30 minutes in a 1-hour window.
- For repeated deviations, we add remediation steps (root cause, mitigations, and a temporary escalation to Dedicated capacity if agreed).

I'll add this language into the RDW-SLA-draft-v1 and flag the warmup/burst limits so Finline can see the guardrails.

-Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2027 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Hosted API commitments and commercial options

Carlos — following up with the commercial framing aligned to the engineering proposal. Summary:

Option A - Standard Hosted (no reserved capacity)
- Commitment: p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 320ms (US region, sliding 1h windows sampled every 5 minutes)
- Credits: service credits tiered: 5% credit if monthly % of failing windows > 0.5%; 15% credit if > 2%.
- Carveouts: up to 8 hours per region per quarter for burst or warmup; scheduled maintenance excluded.

Option B - Premium Hosted (recommended for production clinical workloads)
- Commitment: p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 220ms
- Credits: lower thresholds and smaller credit bands; includes priority capacity and canary buffer.
- SLA addendum available for multi-region failover and 24/7 on-call coordination.

I attached a simple calculator so you can see credit math (SLA-credit-calculator.xlsx). If Finline wants a narrower p95 (e.g., 150ms) we should discuss Reserved/Dedicated to guarantee tail.

Next steps: 1) confirmation of regional scope (US-East only vs all-US), 2) pilot measurement run for 2 weeks to baseline tail numbers, 3) contract addendum.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Carlos Vega <c.vega@finline.com>

Cc: procurement@finline.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commitments and commercial options

Thanks Ben and team — a few follow-ups after reading the draft:

1) Measurement window: Finline prefers commitments measured as a daily aggregated view (we want to avoid hourly volatility impacting credit triggers). Can you map the consequences of switching to daily aggregation of 1h-window samples vs the sliding 1h approach?
2) Regional reporting: we operate multi-az across US-East and US-West; we will need per-region commitments rather than "worst regional value."
3) Carveout caps: can you lower the transient burst allowance to 4 hours per quarter (we're sensitive to tail spikes impacting downstream SLOs).

Also — we need a two-week baseline report on our current traffic pattern against your standard hosted tier before we finalize. Can Redwood run an agreed pilot and produce a short report?

Attached are some internal questions (Finline-SLA-questions.docx). Happy to take a call Thursday.

Regards,
Carlos

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@finline.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Jan 2027 16:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commitments and commercial options — next steps

Carlos — appreciate the specificity. Quick answers and proposed plan:

- Measurement aggregation: we can report both (sliding 1h windows sampled every 5 minutes for operational monitoring, and a daily aggregated view that summarizes worst-performing 1h windows across the day). For contractual credit triggers we can use the daily-aggregated view if that makes you comfortable; we'll show both in the pilot report so you see the delta.
- Regional reporting: agreed to per-region commitments (US-East and US-West) instead of taking the worst regional value. We'll produce two region-level metrics in the addendum.
- Carveout caps: we can meet 4 hours per region per quarter as a contractual cap, provided both parties agree to an incident review process for each carveout.
- Pilot: Redwood will run a two-week production pilot on your traffic (production-sampled quantiles only) starting after PO and with a technical onboarding call to configure sampling. We'll deliver a baseline report and suggested tier placement.

Next steps: 1) Ben to confirm commercial language and pilot terms, 2) Legal to prep an addendum showing per-region commitments and 4-hour carveout cap, 3) Schedule a pilot kickoff (link: https://cal.com/hannah/30m).

I'll mark this as the agreed negotiation points and will loop Legal. Call Thursday sounds good — Ben, can you propose two time slots?

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
